methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses a layered preclinical design (in vitro cytotoxicity across many tumor lines, orthogonal CD226/CD155/PVRIG/CD96 KO rescue experiments, in vivo xenograft models in two tumor types, ddPCR biodistribution, WGS/RNA-seq off-target analysis) that is appropriate and well controlled for the mechanistic claims. Key strengths include the CD226 double-KO rescue (Fig. 3G–J) that genetically supports the proposed inhibitory-to-activating signaling switch, use of three donors for editing efficiency, and genomic safety assessment with WGS and transcriptomics. However, no a priori power calculation is reported for in vivo experiments, randomization and blinding of mouse experiments are not described, missing-data handling is not addressed, and 'at least three repeats' is stated without consistent n reporting per figure. Statistics rely primarily on Student t-test and one-way ANOVA without reporting effect sizes, confidence intervals, or any multiplicity correction despite the many pairwise comparisons across tumor panels and KO combinations.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work is entirely preclinical (primary human NK cells in vitro and xenograft mouse models), placing it at Oxford LoE 5. Despite this, translational relevance is high: TIGIT is a validated clinical target, the platform addresses recognized limitations of anti-TIGIT antibody therapy (fratricide, phase III failures) and NK-cell manufacturing (expansion, cryopreservation for off-the-shelf use), and the authors state the product has already received NMPA and FDA clinical trial clearance for advanced solid tumors. Endpoints (tumor burden by BLI, survival) are standard preclinical surrogates with clear mapping to first-in-human NK-cell trials.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE is the applicable standard given the primary in vivo experiments; the manuscript reports strain/vendor RRIDs, housing/ethics approvals, inoculation doses, and imaging methods, but omits several ARRIVE 2.0 essentials including sample size justification, randomization scheme, blinding of outcome assessment, exclusion criteria, and per-group n for several figures. For the in vitro work, cell line authentication (STR, Mycoplasma, RRIDs) is well handled. Data availability is weak: no accession numbers for the WGS or transcriptome data are stated in the text, no code is referenced, and sgRNA sequences and primers are only referenced to supplementary tables; without an explicit repository deposit this is at best share-on-request.

novelty_literature.justification: Novelty is primarily methodological: application of a cas-embedded cytosine base editor (AccuBase) by RNP electroporation to primary feeder-expanded PB-NK cells to disrupt TIGIT, rather than CRISPR/Cas9 nuclease. The underlying biological concept — that TIGIT KO in NK cells enhances antitumor activity by redirecting CD155 to CD226 — has been established previously (e.g., Hasan 2023 J Immunother Cancer; Zhang 2018 Nat Immunol; Pomeroy 2020 Mol Ther), which the authors appropriately cite. The explicit mechanistic demonstration via CD226 rescue and ERK sustainment is a solid incremental extension, and the integrated off-the-shelf/cryopreservation/biodistribution package is useful, but the paper is not first-in-class conceptually.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a clear logical flow from editing optimization through mechanism, in vivo efficacy, cryopreservation, safety, and biodistribution; figure captions are generally informative and standalone-interpretable. Minor issues include a duplicated 'significance statement' sentence appearing both at the start and end of the abstract, several awkward phrasings (e.g., 'the sharing of ligands... is not a phenomenon observed in NK cells' appears to mean the opposite of what is intended), and some figure-caption/text alignment issues (e.g., K562 written as 'K652' in Fig. 3A caption). Terminology is defined and acronyms expanded appropriately.

key_strengths: High-efficiency (>87%) non-viral base editing of TIGIT in feeder-expanded primary human NK cells with stable phenotype after cryopreservation
Mechanistic rigor: CD226 double-KO rescue and ERK phosphorylation kinetics genetically support the CD155 inhibitory-to-activating signaling switch
Comprehensive safety package including WGS off-target analysis, transcriptomic profiling, histopathology, and ddPCR biodistribution
Clear translational relevance with reported NMPA and FDA IND clearances and off-the-shelf cryopreservation data
Breadth of tumor models tested in vitro (CD155-stratified panel) and in two xenograft models (NSCLC, fibrosarcoma)
key_concerns: No power calculation, randomization scheme, or blinding described for in vivo experiments; per-group n reporting is inconsistent
Statistical analysis is basic (t-test/ANOVA) with no multiplicity correction, effect sizes, or confidence intervals despite many pairwise comparisons

Core biological concept (TIGIT KO in NK cells enhances antitumor activity via CD226) is incremental over Hasan 2023 and Pomeroy 2020; novelty rests mainly on the base-editing/AccuBase delivery platform
Data/code sharing posture is weak: no stated repository accessions for WGS or transcriptome data, no code availability
ARRIVE 2.0 reporting gaps (sample size justification, exclusion criteria, blinded outcome assessment)
Minor presentation issues: duplicated significance statement in abstract, typographical inconsistencies in figure captions
chief_reviewer.rationale: The study is a methodologically solid, mechanistically well-controlled preclinical translational package with clear near-term clinical relevance (reported IND clearances), consistent with a Tier 2 oncology/immunology journal; novelty and reporting-standard gaps keep it below Tier 1.
